scenes.narration: Many mid-career professionals treat their LinkedIn profile as a static biography.

vars.title: Rewrite Your LinkedIn for Future You

scenes.narration: A list of titles, and a vague summary about being an "experienced professional." It sits there. It doesn't do much.

vars.label: The default profile
vars.heading: What Most Profiles Look Like
vars.point1: A list of titles and a vague summary

scenes.narration: But here's the thing: your LinkedIn is one of your most important positioning tools. Recruiters, managers, and peers often see your headline and your "About" section before they see anything else about you.

vars.statement: Your LinkedIn Is a Positioning Tool
vars.lines: One of your most important tools|Recruiters, managers, and peers see it first|Your headline and About section|Before anything else about you

scenes.narration: That's your first impression, and it's working whether you've shaped it or not. So let's shape it.

vars.kicker: Whether you've shaped it or not
vars.lines: It's your first impression|So let's shape it, on purpose

scenes.narration: A strong mid-career headline and summary does three things. First, it speaks to the future roles you're aiming for.
Second, it highlights the strengths and skills you want to be known for.
And third, it shows the value you create, in a way that's clear and human.
For your headline, you can use a simple structure. Target role or direction, then your key strengths and skills, then the value you create or the area you focus on.

vars.label: Headline structure
vars.heading: A Simple Structure for Your Headline
vars.step3: The value you create or focus on

scenes.narration: Separate them with a line, and let each piece do a job. Here's what that shift looks like.

vars.statement: Let Each Piece Do Its Own Job
vars.lines: Separate each part with a line|Here's what that shift looks like

scenes.narration: Before, a headline might read: "Project Manager at X Company." True, but it only names where you've been. After, it becomes: "Senior Program Leader — driving cross-functional initiatives, improving outcomes in higher ed."
Same person. But now the profile points forward. Now for your "About" summary. Think of it as a short narrative rather than a resume dump.

vars.label: Same person, new direction
vars.heading: From This Chapter to the Next
vars.point1: Same person, but the profile now points forward
vars.point2: Write your About summary as a narrative

scenes.narration: It connects your past to your future. It names two or three themes or strengths. And it describes the kind of problems you love to solve, and for whom.

vars.label: The About summary
vars.heading: What a Strong Summary Does
vars.point1: Connects your past to your future
vars.point2: Names two or three themes or strengths
vars.point3: Describes the problems you love to solve, and for whom

scenes.narration: In this module, you'll draft a future-oriented headline and summary.

vars.statement: Draft a Future-Oriented Headline and Summary

scenes.narration: Then use AI feedback to sharpen your positioning, whether you're aiming for a promotion, a lateral move, or a role redesign.

vars.label: Then, sharpen it
vars.heading: Sharpen Your Positioning with AI Feedback

scenes.narration: When you reposition your LinkedIn this way, you make it easier for new doors to open.

vars.statement: New Doors Open When You Reposition

scenes.narration: Because people can immediately see how your experience and strengths match the roles and challenges you're excited about next.

vars.next: See how your experience and strengths match what's next
